title: Update on my AI-made sci-fi game: I furnished an entire moon station, then threw out 221 of the 369 models
author: Exciting-Pool5495
selftext:
*Full disclosure: I am using Tripo to make this game. Which parts are Tripo and which aren't is spelled out below.*

Hey everyone! Another update on **Krakatoa Circle 2**. Before you meet W.A.R.D.E.N., the machine that runs the dig, you walk Asha through a station on the Moon. It had walls, doors, screens and lights, but it didn't look like anyone lived or worked there. Here's how I furnished it, what I got wrong the first time, and how I decided what to do in Blender and what to make with Tripo.

First, a video of two other new things, the walls that seal a fight and the Super Sprint. More on both at the end:

https://reddit.com/link/1y5c91d/video/rkys6tmoes3i1/player

And the station, from the same cameras before and after:

https://i.redd.it/rapr84ppes3i1.jpeg

**How the station was furnished**

The station is seven rooms: the main corridor, receiving, the excavation gallery, operations, a residential hall, the crew's quarters and an equipment store. I tried to make tradeoffs on when to use Tripo and when to have Astra or Claude do it in Blender. Simple things, like chairs, desks, shelves and lockers, are Blender models. For more complex stuff I used Tripo, and that's further down.

The Blender furniture went like this:

1. **Pick.** About 400 searches and 440 downloaded Blender models.
2. **Prepare.** A script cleans each model up, cuts it down to between 300 and 8,000 triangles depending on its size, and bakes it to one texture set.
3. **Place.** A layout script puts every piece on a real surface, then checks it against the walls, the doors, the other pieces, the camera paths of the opening scenes and the player's walking space.
4. **Merge and light.** Everything in a room becomes a few merged chunks that share one texture set. The light of 76 new lamps and all the screens is baked in, with the furniture casting shade on the room.

The station doors are on that side of the line too. No Tripo: Claude built the door and its opening animation in code, and the light on it is baked in Blender, in the same scene as the rooms. The ring charges, the lock turns, the bottom block drops into the floor and the two halves run into the walls. It opens in a bit over half a second, and closes behind you:

https://reddit.com/link/1y5c91d/video/mcxtsvtpes3i1/player

**Then I threw out most of it**

The first version had 369 models and 935 pieces. It was full, and a lot of it was wrong. What gave it away was one prop: a row of airport queue barriers in receiving. Who flew those to the Moon?

So every model had to pass one question: *would a small crew on a sealed lunar dig have flown this up, and would they use it in this room?* 221 of the 369 failed. Among them:

* **54** were living-room furniture and decoration (floor lamps, bookcases, posters).
* **51** were jokes, brands, broken models or things from somewhere else (a smiling robot, a telescope, world maps).
* **35** were wood, cardboard, fuel or rust.
* **22** were paper office (a copier, corkboards, binders).
* **17** came from a public building or a shop (the queue barriers, airport seats, vending machines).
* **17** were from the wrong decade (tube monitors, a boombox).
* **12** belonged in a games room or a bar.

Same room, same camera:

https://i.redd.it/a3298zypes3i1.jpeg

The layout script now enforces this. It refuses a model the review cut, a piece standing alone in the middle of the floor, anything solid in front of a locker, bunk or bench, and anything over one of the station's own screens or signs. Walkable floor for the player went from 559 of 569 square metres to 757 of 763, and the furniture from 1.18 million triangles to about 750,000. With the doors shut a view draws at most about 185,000 of those.

The notices on the walls are now the station's own words (muster points, oxygen, water). And after all that deleting, a few rugs came back where people sit, eat and work.

**Where Tripo comes in: the dig site**

The complex stuff is outside the station, in the Dig Site: a shotcrete sprayer, a containment pod, an ancient slab strapped to a pallet. The last round added 48 new models, 37 of them made with Tripo, as a small kit for each zone, so the hangar, the tunnel, the benches and the pit stop looking the same:

https://i.redd.it/ne1nin4qes3i1.jpeg

Each one starts as a ChatGPT picture of a single object, with a crop of my reference painting of that zone as the style guide. Then it's one image-to-3D call. This is the call for the drill rig, with the Tripo CLI:

    tripo generate image-to-model blasthole_drill_rig.png \
      --model tripo-p2 \
      -p face_limit=30000 -p texture=true -p pbr=true \
      -p texture_quality=standard \
      -p texture_alignment=original_image

That's 110 credits a model with these settings. The models then go through my own steps (size, facing, distance versions, collision) and the placement script swapped about 1,100 repeated copies for new kinds.

If you want to try it, here's the [Tripo API documentation](https://developers.tripo3d.ai/en/docs). The [quick start](https://developers.tripo3d.ai/en/docs/quick-start) gets you a key and a first request, and this is the [image-to-3D page for the P series](https://developers.tripo3d.ai/en/docs/generation-image-to-model/p) I used.

**What's in the first video**

**The fight walls.** When a fight starts, the road is sealed. It used to be a bright energy field, which looked wrong in a dark cosmic horror game. Now threads of sinew are laid one at a time into a net, flesh grows over them, and the thing inside follows you and throws itself at the other side. When you win, it's pulled apart along its seams. It has no light of its own, so you only see it by the lamps of the place. This is all procedural: baked maps, shaders and a few hundred ribbons, no generated models.

**The Super Sprint.** Three times her normal sprint, in long slow bounds instead of faster legs. Each bound is about 18 metres. The energy builds with every strike and peaks after three seconds. The animation is written in code too.

**What worked**

* Asking "who brought this here, and who uses it?" of every prop. It's a much better test than "does it look good?"
* Making the review a rule in the script, so a cut prop can't come back.
* One object per picture, before image-to-3D.
* Giving each zone its own kit. The old level used one truck 398 times.

**What didn't**

* Density. I filled rooms with recognisable things, and they looked busy instead of lived in.
* Flight suits on hangers. From across the room they read as invisible people. A medical couch read as a bathtub.
* Open racks in image-to-3D. The drone rack in the picture above came back with a wall across its middle.
* A wall lamp a few centimetres from its panel set the brightest point of the whole light map. The walls were left with a handful of brightness levels, and every panel had a pink and green film over it.

I'd love to hear what you think. Does the station read as a place people work? And when do you generate a model, and when do you just do it in Blender?
